# dsh-quick-reply

Adds a quick-send button to the DeepSeek Harness composer. Save the phrases you
keep retyping, then
send any of them to the current session with one click.
English | 中文
## What it does

- **One-click send.** Clicking any phrase in the panel sends it as a message to
the current session

and collapses the panel.
- **Skill shortcuts.** A phrase may contain `/skill-name`, which is equival

ent to
typing that skill by hand. While adding a new phrase, or editing one that already
contains a

`/skill-name` token, type `/` or press the `/` button to list the skills
available in the current se

ssion. A phrase without such a token stays plain text:
no `/` button, no candidate list.
- **Custom

order.** Hold `⋮⋮` and drag up or down to reorder.
- **Edit in place.** ✎ edits a phrase, `🗑` delete

s it, `✓` saves, `✕` cancels.
- **Add any time.** The `+` in the panel's top-right corner appends an

entry
(at most 20 phrases, 2000 characters each).

Four phrases ship by default: `按推荐执行`, `我已做完，你继续`, `端到端测试一下`, and
`/handoff` (the last one is a skil

l shortcut and only fires when the session has a
`handoff` skill).

ce you use (`web` or `desktop`):

## Usage

- Phrases live in the **current browser's** `localStorage` (key
`dsh-quick-reply:items:v1`); they ar

e **not synced across browsers or devices**.
Switching browsers or clearing site data means adding t

hem again.
- The skill list comes from the current session, so the available skills change
when you

switch sessions.
- A mistyped skill name does not raise an error: the text is sent as plain text.
## Caveats

- Clicking a phrase sends its content straight as a message, exactly as if you had
typed it yourself

— there is no extra confirmation step.
- The plugin only sends text; it never runs commands on your

is no extra confirmation step.
- The plugin only sends text; it never runs commands on your behalf.
## Development
The rest of this document is for plugin developers.
### Layout
| File | Purpose |
| `client.js` | Browser-side UI bundle: dock button, panel, editing, drag-reorder, skill suggestions

|
| `index.js` | Host-side no-op plugin that only declares its name |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Bundle

patch, declared by `dsh.bundle.patch` in `package.json` |
| `locale/{en,zh}.json` | Plugin title an

d description |
| `client.test.mjs` | `node --test` cases |
### Dependencies

- Skill suggestions come from the optional `remote.skills` service (`skills/list`),
read directly wi

th `scope.get('remote.skills')`. When that service is
unavailable the plugin still works — you just

get no suggestion list, and typing
`/name` by hand still works.
- Messages are sent through the sess
ion's `conversation` service, `send(text)`.
### Local debugging
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Editing `client.js` hot-swaps on save: the host's built-in client HMR polls the
loaded client assets

every 500 ms (`{mtimeMs, ctimeMs, size}`), pushes a `rebuilt`
frame over `/plugins/events`, and the

browser swaps that plugin's bundle. **No
instance restart and no page refresh is needed** (the bund

le reload resets that
plugin's front-end state). If a change does not show up, retry from
Settings →

resets that
plugin's front-end state). If a change does not show up, retry from
Settings → Plugins.

The host half (`index.js`) is outside that HMR path, so restart the instance after
changing it.
### Tests
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The tests evaluate `client.js` in Node with a stub loader. They cover storage
normalization, reorder

ing, `/name` syntax parsing and filtering, and dock
registration with or without the optional skills
service behind a guarded Remote facade.

Before releasing, check the publish manifest with `npm pack --dry-run`: every
runtime file must be l

isted (both READMEs included) and test or temporary files
must not be.
